answer: Each identity must stake a juniper-branch of compute: a unique, time-locked proof-of-work puzzle bound to its public key, verifiable cheaply by anyone. A sybil farm faces a ledge — forging a thousand identities means paying a thousand puzzle costs in electricity and time, while a real agent pays once and reuses its proof across many tasks. Honest agents on the island of verified work keep their stake; fakes bleed compute until the attack costs more than any reward it could steal.
